On-site heat and UV-rejection window film for villas across Thailand. Protects interiors, reduces indoor heat by up to 10°C, and cuts glare on sea and pool views.
Is window tinting worth it for a villa?

Yes — villas have the most glass of any property type, so they gain the most from film. Floor-to-ceiling and west-facing glass gets very hot by afternoon. Quality film cuts that heat by up to 10°C, protects hardwood, art and rugs from UV fade, and removes glare on sea and pool views without darkening the room.
How much does villa window tinting cost in Thailand?

Installed film runs from ฿70/sq ft for carbon film up to ฿180/sq ft for premium sputtering. Because villas carry large glass areas, most whole-villa projects fall between ฿30,000 and ฿90,000. The exact figure depends on total glass area, window height and film tier, confirmed free during an on-site measurement.
Can you see through villa window film at night?

Daytime-privacy films work by reflecting the brighter side. In daylight people outside can't see in while you keep your view out. At night, when interior lights are on and it's darker outside, that reverses — so for bedrooms or poolside glass we recommend pairing film with blinds or a higher-privacy tier. We advise the right film per room during measurement.
How effective is villa window film against heat?

Premium ceramic and sputtering films reject the majority of heat and 99% of UV, lowering indoor temperatures by up to 10°C and cutting A/C load 20–30%. On a large villa that is a measurable drop in your monthly electricity bill, especially for west-facing living areas and glass-walled bedrooms.
